title: Inside a peripheral nerve
objective: Name the connective-tissue layers of a peripheral nerve and explain that most nerves are mixed.

steps.title: A cable of cables
steps.body:
A peripheral nerve is a bundle, wrapped in three sheaths:

- **[[endoneurium]]** wraps each individual axon
- **[[perineurium]]** binds axons into a **[[fascicle]]**
- **[[epineurium]]** wraps the whole nerve

Most nerves are **mixed**: sensory ([[afferent]]) and motor ([[efferent]]) axons travel together.

steps.prompt: Order the nerve wrappings from the single axon outward.
steps.explanation: Endoneurium → perineurium → epineurium: innermost to outermost. The perineurium also forms a protective barrier around each fascicle.

steps.prompt: A nerve is described as 'mixed'. What does that mean?
options: It carries both sensory and motor axons together
It belongs to the central nervous system
It carries both sympathetic and parasympathetic axons
steps.explanation: A mixed nerve carries [[afferent]] (sensory) and [[efferent]] (motor) axons in the same bundle — so one cut can affect both.

variants.setup: A nerve contains both afferent and efferent axons.
variants.reveal: Carrying both sensory and motor fibers makes it a mixed nerve.

steps.setup: A mixed nerve to a limb is crushed.
steps.prompt: What do you predict for that limb?
options: Only movement is affected, sensation is spared
Both sensation and movement can be lost in its territory
Only sensation is affected, movement is spared
steps.reveal: Because the nerve carries both afferent and efferent axons, a lesion can knock out sensation *and* movement in the area it serves.

variants.prompt: Crushing a mixed nerve can impair…
options: Both sensation and movement in its territory
Only sensation, with movement fully spared
Only movement, with sensation fully spared
variants.explanation: Mixed nerves carry sensory and motor axons, so both can be lost.

reviewNotes: Nerve structure and mixed nerves; sets up conduction and lesions.
